title: Client priority hypotheses and request synthesis - Jul 2026
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact working synthesis of high-frequency customer feedback from Q2->early Jul 2026 (support tickets, top-10 customers interviews, account exec notes, NPS comments). The goal is to convert noisy asks into testable product hypotheses and short-term engineering workstreams.

Sources & scope:
- Support tickets (May 1 - Jul 5): ~420 tickets tagged model-choice, latency, rollout, private-deploy
- 10 targeted customer interviews (CS-led, median ARR = $1.2M)
- 3 sales-qualified demos notes and post-demo follow-ups
- Internal Slack threads (cs-biz, eng-rt): synthesis channel export

High-level signal summary (top emergent themes):
1) Predictable latency under bursty loads (MVP ask: graceful capacity buffer).
   - Pain: customers experience periodic 500-800ms latency spikes when traffic bursts; affects UI perception for chat apps.
   - Impact: high (customer churn / bad UX).
   - Frequency: high among mid-market and growth SaaS.

2) Easier model fallback / hybrid routing policies.
   - Pain: teams want a declarative way to say “prefer base model A, fall back to lightweight B at X latency threshold or cost target.”
   - Impact: medium-high (cost and uptime safety).

3) More granular, per-endpoint token cost visibility in Console and API responses.
   - Pain: billing reconciliation is hard when customers use many models/variants; token attribution across rollouts unclear.
   - Impact: medium (finance + SRE planning).

4) Private deployment onboarding friction: network config and KMS flow.
   - Pain: customers stuck during setup, long discovery calls.
   - Impact: high for enterprise deals.

5) Quality regression alerts tied to canonical eval prompts.
   - Pain: customers want automatic regression detection when model version changes or quantization profiles applied.
   - Impact: high for teams with safety/regulatory SLAs.

Notable verbatim quotes (useful for PR/exec memos):
- "We can survive a 10% increase in tail latency once a week, but not unpredictable spikes during peak." — Head of Platform, fintech customer
- "Rolling back a model is our only safety valve today; we need something smarter we can automate." — ML engineer, mid-market customer
- "I spend an extra day every month reconciling invoices because of model variants — please give me per-route spend." — FP&A lead, edtech customer

Consolidated feature request list (working IDs and short hypotheses):
FR-101: Soft-capacity buffer (server-side burst pool)
- Hypothesis: A short-lived burst pool (configurable per-dedicated instance) will reduce 95/99th percentile token latency during traffic spikes without large steady-state cost impact.
- Observed pain: repeated burst-induced tail latency spikes.
- Sample customers: handful of chat-first startups, 2 enterprise accounts with predictable daily peaks.
- Suggested priority: P0 for dedicated customers; P1 for hosted API.
- Implementation notes (rough): scheduler + token-bucket priority; metrics delta to validate: 95th/99th token latency pre/post and cost delta per 100k tokens.

FR-115: Declarative fallback routing rules (latency/cost targets)
- Hypothesis: Exposing a simple rules DSL (e.g., threshold -> fallback model) will reduce manual rollback incidents and lower cost by automatically routing cheap variant for non-critical requests.
- Observed pain: manual rollbacks and ad-hoc client logic.
- Sample customers: two scale-up SaaS apps using Redwood routing today.
- Suggested priority: P0 (valuable for both hosted + dedicated).

FR-127: Per-route spend breakdown and token attribution export
- Hypothesis: Adding per-route token attribution in Console and a CSV export will reduce finance tickets and time-to-reconcile invoices by >50% for customers in pilot.
- Observed pain: opaque billing for multi-model rollouts.
- Suggested priority: P1.

FR-140: Private onboarding checklist + network preflight tool
- Hypothesis: A checklist + lightweight preflight that validates common KMS/VPC settings will reduce onboarding time by ~40% and shorten deal close cycles.
- Observed pain: repeated discovery calls and misconfigured customer networks.
- Suggested priority: P0 for sales-assisted private deals.

FR-152: Eval-watch (auto regression alerts on eval sets)
- Hypothesis: If we attach eval suites to model rollouts and generate alerts when quality drops beyond a chosen threshold, customers will trust automated rollouts more and reduce manual gating.
- Observed pain: fears of hidden regressions from quantization/model swaps.
- Suggested priority: P0 for enterprise customers, P1 for hosted.

Quick validation experiments (low-effort tactical wins):
- Experiment A (1-week): Internal beta of per-endpoint spend CSV for 5 customers — measure support tickets reduction. Owner: Priya.
- Experiment B (2-week): Add a console toggle that simulates fallback routing for a single route (no infra change) and collect feedback from 3 customers. Owner: Owen.
- Experiment C (2-week): Run a private-onboarding war-room for next 3 customers and track repeated failure modes; build preflight checklist. Owner: Lucas.

Risk notes & unresolved questions (short):
- Cost/benefit model: Soft buffers may increase burst cost; we need to quantify unit economics per GPU family. Who in Eng infra can help with a quick sim?
- UX surface: How do we expose fallback DSL without confusing existing customers using custom routing? (Need design/PD input.)
- Data privacy: Eval-watch will require storing customer prompts/labels — compliance checks needed for regulated customers.

Next steps (12 business day cadence suggested):
1) Align CS + Eng-Serving on P0 list (FR-101, FR-115, FR-140, FR-152) — 2d sync. Owner: Maya.
2) Kick Experiment A/B within 5 business days. Priya/Owen.
3) Engage infra kernel team to estimate cost model for burst pools. Request ticket: JIRA-3421.
4) Draft simple fallback DSL spec (1-pager) and circulate to 2 customers for feedback. Owner: Owen.
5) Build Private onboarding preflight MVP (checklist + basic network tests) and pilot on 2 deals. Owner: Lucas.

Notes to self / open bullets to capture in follow-up doc:
- Capture sample logs showing tail-latency pre/post for next 3 incidents and anonymize for infra analysis.
- Create single place in Confluence to store canonical eval prompts per customer (link above) and define retention policy.
- Consider adding a finance-facing UI walkthrough to Console help center for FR-127.

Appendix: Raw counts (quick):
- Tickets citing latency/burst: 128 (30% of sampled tickets)
- Tickets citing billing/attribution: 47 (11%)
- Tickets citing private onboarding: 63 (15%)
- Interview quotes supporting eval-watch: 8/10 interviews mentioned quality/regression worries

If you want this converted into a one-pager for GTM or a tech spec for Eng-Serving, say so and I’ll author next drafts.

-- Maya
